Serializer accepts reports with neither age nor timestamp
The old BrowserReport dataclass required `timestamp`. The new serializer makes both `age` and `timestamp` optional. The validators only reject the case where both are present, and they only run when their field is supplied. A report with neither field, such as `{"body":{},"type":"crash","url":"https://a.com","user_agent":"x","destination":"default","attempts":1}`, now passes validation. get_committable_offsets walks range(start, max_offset+1) and breaks at the first offset that is not in all_offsets (lines 89-93). Offsets never submitted to the tracker are not tracked. These include Kafka offset gaps from compaction or transaction markers, and any message that does not reach submit. Such an offset is treated as a hole, so the loop breaks there on every pass.

Commits highest processed offset instead of next offset to consume
get_committable_offsets returns the highest fully processed offset (line 96), and _commit_loop passes that dict unchanged to commit_function. Arroyo/Kafka commit semantics expect the next offset to consume (processed offset + 1). Offset N, which has already been processed, is therefore committed as the resume position. mark_committed then records N as last_committed, so the tracker and Kafka agree on the same off-by-one value.
